newsitem.title: GERMANY: All have same opportunity to join EMU -- Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: All have same opportunity to join EMU -- Kinkel.

text.p: All European Union member states will get the same chance to join a planned EU single currency in 1999 if they fulfil the economic criteria, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Monday.
"Any member state can qualify to join European economic and monetary union (EMU)," Kinkel said in a statement after meeting his Austrian counterpart, Wolfgang Schuessel.
"There is no pecking order of member countries. The only deciding factor is the strict, sustainable fulfilment of the (Maastricht) treaty conditions," he added.

Senior German bankers have recently warned of turmoil in financial markets if Mediterranean countries like Italy, whose currencies have been less stable than the mark, are allowed to join EMU when it starts in 1999, even if they fulfil the criteria.

This has prompted Spain and Italy to state emphatically that they expect to be judged purely and simply on whether they fulfil the treaty criteria, something even Germany is struggling to achieve, and irrespective of other considerations.
The statement said both Kinkel and Schuessel wanted as many countries as possible to join EMU, but insisted that the criteria would not be relaxed.
It said both men agreed that the single currency must start on schedule on January 1, 1999, and that it would fulfil all the conditions to be every bit as stable as the German mark.
